flags.name: profile
flags.usage: profile name to connect (see ~/.many-ai-cli/launcher-profiles.yaml)

flags.name: last
flags.usage: connect using the last-used profile

flags.name: json
flags.usage: output as JSON

flags.name: name
flags.usage: profile display name (default: hostname)

flags.name: host
flags.usage: public host to advertise first (overrides auto-detected IP; e.g. for Docker)

flags.name: cwd
flags.usage: remote working directory (default: current directory)

flags.name: hub-port
flags.usage: fixed hub port (0 = auto-select)

flags.name: json
flags.usage: output as JSON

flags.name: o
flags.usage: output transcript path

flags.name: purge
flags.usage: バイナリ本体も削除する

flags.name: role
flags.usage: child role (required, e.g. implementation/test/review)

flags.name: provider
flags.usage: override provider; one of claude|codex|copilot|cursor-agent|opencode|grok (exact lowercase). Default: the role mapping decided at conductor launch, then the provider last used for this role, then the parent's provider

flags.name: model
flags.usage: override model (default: resolved from the role mapping decided at conductor launch)

flags.name: cwd
flags.usage: root for the child's working directory (default: parent session cwd). By default many-ai-cli creates an orchestration worktree under this directory and the child runs there, not directly in this directory; pass -same-tree to have the child run in this directory itself

flags.name: same-tree
flags.usage: run the child directly in -cwd instead of an orchestration worktree (default: use a worktree; the child then edits your working tree directly, so do not edit it in parallel)

flags.name: force
flags.usage: spawn a new child even if a live child already exists for the role (default: rejected; use `orchestrate send` instead)

flags.name: effort
flags.usage: reasoning effort for the child; accepted values depend on the provider (claude: low|medium|high|xhigh|max, codex: minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max, opencode: the model's own variant name). Providers without an effort flag (copilot / cursor-agent / grok / command-code / custom) reject a non-empty value

flags.name: execution-mode
flags.usage: auto|interactive|headless (default: auto). headless runs the child through the provider's own non-interactive mode and needs a definition for that provider; asking for it where there is none is rejected rather than quietly downgraded

flags.name: permission
flags.usage: attended|bounded|full (default: the orchestration child default). attended sends the child's approval prompts to the Hub's approval panel; bounded runs the allowlisted actions without asking and denies the rest (copilot has no auto-deny, so there anything outside the list still prompts); full allows everything

flags.name: role
flags.usage: target child role (required)

flags.name: plan
flags.usage: plan markdown path (required)

flags.name: max-rounds
flags.usage: maximum review rounds per C (default: 3)

flags.name: impl
flags.usage: implementation provider[/model][@effort]

flags.name: review
flags.usage: review provider[/model][@effort]

flags.name: strong
flags.usage: strong implementation provider[/model][@effort]

flags.name: escalate-after
flags.usage: failed review rounds before strong implementation (default: 2)

flags.name: same-tree
flags.usage: run children in the parent's working tree

flags.name: extra-impl
flags.usage: extra instructions for the implementation role

flags.name: extra-review
flags.usage: extra instructions for the review role

flags.name: execution-mode
flags.usage: auto|interactive|headless for every relay role (default: orchestration.relay_execution_mode, itself unset = interactive). headless runs each instruction as one non-interactive process of the provider's own print mode and takes its exit as the completion signal; a role whose provider has no headless definition is rejected here rather than quietly run interactively

flags.name: permission
flags.usage: attended|bounded|full for every relay role (default: orchestration.child_permission_default). attended sends the child's approval prompts to the Hub's approval panel, which nobody is watching during an unattended relay; bounded runs the allowlisted actions without asking and denies the rest (copilot has no auto-deny, so there anything outside the list still prompts); full allows everything

flags.name: id
flags.usage: show only this orchestration id

flags.name: id
flags.usage: orchestration id (optional when exactly one relay is active)

flags.name: provider
flags.usage: provider: claude or codex

flags.name: hub
flags.usage: Hub base URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:47777)

flags.name: token
flags.usage: Hub auth token (deprecated: use MANY_AI_CLI_HUB_TOKEN env instead)

flags.name: session
flags.usage: session ID

flags.name: label
flags.usage: session label shown in UI card

flags.name: model
flags.usage: model override

flags.name: permission-mode
flags.usage: permission mode (claude/grok: passed through; copilot auto→--autopilot bypass→--allow-all; cursor-agent auto→--auto-review bypass→--force; opencode bypass→--auto; command-code plan→--permission-mode plan, acceptEdits/auto→--auto-accept, bypass→--yolo)

flags.name: effort
flags.usage: reasoning effort (claude: --effort; codex: -c model_reasoning_effort; opencode: --variant; others: ignored)

flags.name: allowed-tools
flags.usage: bounded tier allowlist, comma-separated (claude: --allowedTools values; copilot: --allow-tool values; others: ignored)

flags.name: sandbox
flags.usage: codex sandbox mode

flags.name: ask-for-approval
flags.usage: codex ask-for-approval

flags.name: codex-oss
flags.usage: codex: use --oss to route via local Ollama daemon

flags.name: utf8
flags.usage: set UTF-8 console encoding for this session (Windows only)

flags.name: subscription-login
flags.usage: run the provider CLI's own login flow instead of an interactive session

flags.name: headless
flags.usage: run the provider's own non-interactive mode (no PTY) instead of an interactive session; requires a headless definition for the provider

flags.name: prompt-file
flags.usage: file holding the initial prompt. The wrapper reads it once and deletes it. Headless: passed the way the provider's headless definition says. Interactive: passed as the CLI's first launch argument, or as a one-line pointer to a private file when the launch goes through cmd.exe or the prompt is very long (launch_prompt.go)

  -force orchestrate send
    	spawn a new child even if a live child already exists for the role (default: rejected; use orchestrate send instead)

  -provider string
    	override provider; one of claude|codex|copilot|cursor-agent|opencode|grok (exact lowercase). Default: the role mapping decided at conductor launch, then the provider last used for this role, then the parent's provider

    	child role (required, e.g. implementation/test/review)
  -same-tree
